title: An eval bank scores every task it holds with no per-task validity attestation, so a defective task is billed to the agent
problem: My agent scores 41 percent on my task bank and I cannot tell you how many of the 59 percent it missed were tasks that no correct agent could ever have passed, because nothing in the bank records whether a task was ever checked for being solvable.
symptom: A pass rate that moves when someone rewrites a task or a grader rather than when the agent changes; recurring failures that on inspection turn out to be an ambiguous prompt or a grader asserting a detail the prompt never stated, and no record of which tasks were already known to be like that.
why_now: The two largest public audits of agentic benchmarks both found task validity, not agent capability, to be the dominant error term, and both had to add a human attestation pass to fix it. Yet the attestation is a property of THEIR dataset release, not a field any in-house bank carries, so every team that builds its own bank re-inherits the defect and has no way to report which tasks were vetted.
existing: Publishing a curated subset such as a verified split: fixes one public dataset at one point in time and does nothing for an in-house bank, and the attestation is not carried per task in a form a harness can enforce.
Flakiness quarantine borrowed from CI: catches a task that fails intermittently, but a consistently unsolvable task is not flaky, it is stably wrong, so quarantine never fires on it.
Manual triage of failures each release: finds defective tasks, but the finding lives in a ticket or a person's head rather than in the task record, so the next run scores the same broken task again.

evidence.title: Introducing SWE-bench Verified
evidence.quote: We see that 38.3% of samples were flagged for underspecified problem statements, and 61.1% were flagged for unit tests that may unfairly mark valid solutions as incorrect.
evidence.note: A first-party measurement of the size of the error term. 93 developers annotated 1,699 samples of a benchmark in wide production use, and the majority of samples carried a validity defect; the same page states that 68.3% of samples were filtered out. That is the quantity an unattested bank silently attributes to the agent.

evidence.title: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
evidence.quote: However, we show that many agentic benchmarks have issues in task setup or reward design. For example, SWE-bench Verified uses insufficient test cases, while TAU-bench counts empty responses as successful.
evidence.note: Classified survey-aggregate rather than peer-reviewed deliberately: the arXiv abstract page lists no venue, only page and figure counts, and the paper describes itself as synthesised from a survey of best practices and previously reported issues. It establishes that the defect survives curation - the already-verified split is one of its examples - so a one-off human pass is not a substitute for a per-task attestation the harness enforces.

build_hypothesis: One required field on the task record plus one refusal in the harness. Every task carries a validity attestation (who checked it, when, solvable yes or no, and the reason if not), and the harness refuses to put an unattested or attested-unsolvable task in the denominator, reporting the held-out set alongside the score. The smallest useful version is a linter over an existing bank that prints what fraction of tasks carry no attestation and what the pass rate becomes when those are excluded.

check.manual_question: For your eval bank: which tasks has a human attested are actually solvable and unambiguously specified, and where is that attestation recorded? If the answer is nowhere, you cannot tell a failing agent from a broken task, and your denominator is wrong by an unknown amount.
check.rationale: A repo that ships an eval bank but carries no validity vocabulary anywhere in its code or data has no per-task attestation, so its denominator includes tasks nobody ever checked. The mitigation deliberately requires two things: the attestation vocabulary AND evidence that something acts on it, because a field nobody enforces leaves the broken task in the score. Markdown is excluded from the absence search on purpose - a README discussing task quality is not a recorded per-task label. Known failure modes: a bank that names the field outside this vocabulary reads as mitigated when it is not, and a repo that uses the word solvable or annotator for an unrelated purpose while also having enforcement-shaped text reads as mitigated, which is why the manual question asks where the attestation is recorded rather than trusting the lexical hit.
